<!--
What it does: The review's progress, step by step, as one interactive page.
  1. The 2022 World Bank NbS extraction, African studies: the scope of the
     data, how many years each paper reports an outcome for, a chosen paper's
     values over its years and seasons, and what its costs include.
  2. The practices: Pete Steward's practice vocabulary.
  3. The OpenAlex search: hits per practice and outcome.
  4. Title and abstract screening: a table per search, and the person's QC
     of the model. Records
     with no abstract anywhere are left out for now.
  5. Next steps: full texts through Zotero, then extraction and its QC.
Reads: data/wb_nbs_extraction_2022_cc4a.xlsx           (sheet extracted_cc4a)
       catalogues/vocab_practices.csv                   the practice vocabulary
       docs/synthesis/key-words.xlsx                    search practice names
       outputs/01_search/search_counts.csv              hits per search
       outputs/01_search/search_records_vs_wb2022.csv   DOI and open access
       outputs/03_screen/screen_scope.csv               decisions and QC
Writes: the rendered HTML, docs/reports/progress_report.html when built with
  R/progress_report/render_progress_report.R
Flags: none. Knit in RStudio, or run R/progress_report/render_progress_report.R.
-->

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
                      fig.width = 10, fig.height = 4.5, out.width = "100%")
root <- rprojroot::find_root(rprojroot::has_file("CC4A.Rproj"))
source(file.path(root, "R/00_shared/paths.R"))
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr)
  library(tidyr)
  library(plotly)
  library(crosstalk)
  library(DT)
})

# Money outcomes, which the outcome filter offers. Ratios and rates (benefit
# cost ratios, IRR, NPV ...) appear in the scope chart only.
COST_OUTCOMES <- c("Variable Cost", "Total Cost", "Total Cost (Unconfirmed)", "Labour Cost",
                   "Variable Cost per Asset", "Variable Cost per Unit Product",
                   "Total Cost per Asset", "Total Cost per Unit Product",
                   "Labour Cost per Asset", "Labour Cost per Unit Product",
                   "Present Value of Cost")
RETURN_OUTCOMES <- c("Gross Return", "Net Return", "Net Return (Unconfirmed)", "Gross Margin",
                     "Returns to Labour", "Return to Labour", "Present Value of Benefit")

# The outcome the page opens on.
DEFAULT_OUTCOME <- "Variable Cost"

# Cost item columns in the extraction: yes/no flags for what a cost includes.
COST_ITEMS <- c("Seeds", "Nutrient Inputs", "Labour", "Pest Control Inputs", "Land (rent)",
                "Equipment Costs", "Tax", "Transport", "Irrigation")
COST_ITEM_SHORT <- c("seed", "fertiliser", "labour", "pest control", "land",
                     "equipment", "tax", "transport", "irrigation")

PRACTICE_LABELS <- c(
  awd = "AWD (irrigated rice)", biochar = "Biochar", ca_bundle = "Reduced tillage / CA",
  dsr = "Direct-seeded rice", feed_mgmt = "Feed management",
  nutrient_mgmt_b = "Nutrient management / ISFM", rotational_grazing = "Rotational grazing",
  silvopasture = "Silvopasture", soil_cover = "Soil cover", sri = "SRI",
  trees_in_farmlands = "Trees in farmlands"
)

COL_TREATMENT <- "#1f6fb4"
COL_CONTROL <- "#7f7f7f"
HOW_COLOURS <- c("A separate value for each season" = "#08519c",
                 "A separate value for each year" = "#4292c6",
                 "One value pooled over the years" = "#fdae61",
                 "One year" = "#bdbdbd")

# The three outcome blocks of the search (docs/synthesis/key-words.xlsx).
OUTCOME_LABELS <- c(outcome1 = "Adoption", outcome2 = "Costs, returns and incentives",
                    outcome3 = "Carbon finance")

# Where each screened record ends up, in the order the counts list
# them. A record a person checked at QC follows the person's decision.
SCREEN_GROUPS <- c(
  not_africa = "Not in Africa",
  review = "Review or meta-analysis (kept for citation chasing)",
  no_practice = "No listed practice studied",
  no_outcome = "No cost, adoption or carbon income evidence",
  other_type = "Not a field, survey, evaluation or economic study",
  qc_excluded = "Excluded by a person at QC",
  title_only = "Title only, no abstract yet",
  unsure = "Unsure, for a person",
  included = "Included for full text"
)
EXCLUDE_GROUPS <- names(SCREEN_GROUPS)[1:6]
# The screening rule (R/03_screen/screen_scope.R) behind each model exclusion.
EXCLUDE_RULES <- c(
  "exclude: not in Africa" = "not_africa",
  "exclude: review (keep for citation chasing)" = "review",
  "exclude: no listed practice studied" = "no_practice",
  "exclude: no cost, adoption or carbon income evidence" = "no_outcome",
  "exclude: not a field, survey, evaluation or economic study" = "other_type"
)
```

```{r data}
raw <- readxl::read_excel(FILE_WB2022_CC4A, sheet = "extracted_cc4a", col_types = "text")

#' TRUE where any country named in the cell is in Africa ("Bangladesh/India/
#' Nepal" names three). Looked up once per distinct cell.
is_africa <- function(country) {
  cells <- unique(ifelse(is.na(country), "", country))
  hit <- vapply(strsplit(cells, "[/;,]"), function(p) {
    cont <- suppressWarnings(countrycode::countrycode(trimws(p), "country.name", "continent"))
    any(cont %in% "Africa", na.rm = TRUE)
  }, TRUE)
  unname(setNames(hit, cells)[ifelse(is.na(country), "", country)])
}

#' Years a measurement covers. The column mixes formats: 2017; lists such as
#' 2017.2018; seasons such as 2018.1 or 2018.2.2019.2; ranges such as
#' 2009-2019; and Excel damage such as 2016.2017000000001 or 2009.201
#' (2009.2010 with its trailing zero dropped).
parse_years <- function(s) {
  s <- trimws(s)
  if (is.na(s) || !grepl("(19|20)[0-9]{2}", s)) return(integer())
  if (grepl("^[0-9]{4} *- *[0-9]{4}$", s)) {
    r <- as.integer(strsplit(s, " *- *")[[1]])
    return(seq(min(r), max(r)))
  }
  if (grepl("^[0-9]{4}[.][0-9]{9,}$", s)) {
    second <- round(as.numeric(paste0("0.", substring(s, 6))) * 1e4)
    return(unique(c(as.integer(substr(s, 1, 4)), as.integer(second))))
  }
  if (grepl("^[0-9]{4}[.][0-9]{3}$", s)) {
    return(unique(c(as.integer(substr(s, 1, 4)), as.integer(paste0(substring(s, 6), "0")))))
  }
  tok <- strsplit(s, "[.;,/ ]+")[[1]]
  unique(as.integer(tok[grepl("^(19|20)[0-9]{2}$", tok)]))
}

#' The season of a single-season measurement such as 2017.2, or NA.
season_of <- function(raw_year) {
  ifelse(grepl("^[0-9]{4}[.][1-3]$", trimws(raw_year)),
         as.integer(substring(trimws(raw_year), 6)), NA_integer_)
}

#' Short text saying which cost items a cost includes, for example
#' "seed, labour; not land". `d` holds the COST_ITEMS columns of one or more
#' rows; an item counts as included when any row says yes.
items_text <- function(d) {
  v <- as.matrix(d[, COST_ITEMS])
  yes <- COST_ITEMS[apply(v, 2, function(x) any(grepl("^\\(?yes", x, ignore.case = TRUE)))]
  no <- setdiff(COST_ITEMS[apply(v, 2, function(x) any(grepl("^no", x, ignore.case = TRUE)))], yes)
  short <- setNames(COST_ITEM_SHORT, COST_ITEMS)
  out <- c(if (length(yes)) paste(short[yes], collapse = ", "),
           if (length(no)) paste("not", paste(short[no], collapse = ", ")))
  if (length(out)) paste(out, collapse = "; ") else "not recorded"
}
items_by_row <- function(d) {
  vapply(seq_len(nrow(d)), function(i) items_text(d[i, , drop = FALSE]), "")
}

practice_text <- function(codes) {
  vapply(strsplit(codes, "; "), function(p) {
    l <- PRACTICE_LABELS[p]; l[is.na(l)] <- p[is.na(l)]; paste(l, collapse = "; ")
  }, "")
}

# Africa only, from the start.
af <- raw |>
  filter(is_africa(Country)) |>
  mutate(
    years = lapply(Measurement_Year, parse_years),
    n_years = lengths(years),
    year_first = vapply(years, function(y) if (length(y)) min(y) else NA_integer_, 1L),
    year_last = vapply(years, function(y) if (length(y)) max(y) else NA_integer_, 1L),
    season = ifelse(n_years == 1, season_of(Measurement_Year), NA_integer_),
    unit = trimws(Outcome_Unit),
    value_trt = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(Value_Trt)),
    value_con = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(Value_Con)),
    practices = practice_text(cc4a_practices),
    paper = paste0(Country, ": ", substr(Title, 1, 75), ifelse(nchar(Title) > 75, "...", ""),
                   " [", StudyID, "]"),
    where = trimws(paste(coalesce(Site_Name, ""), coalesce(Product, ""), sep = ", "),
                   whitespace = "[ ,]")
  )

money <- af |>
  filter(Outcome %in% c(COST_OUTCOMES, RETURN_OUTCOMES)) |>
  mutate(items = items_by_row(pick(all_of(COST_ITEMS))))
```

```{r screening-data}
#' Read only the named columns of a pipeline CSV, every column as text.
read_cols <- function(path, cols) {
  readr::read_csv(path, col_types = readr::cols(.default = readr::col_character()),
                  col_select = all_of(cols), na = "", progress = FALSE,
                  show_col_types = FALSE)
}

keywords <- readxl::read_excel(FILE_KEYWORDS_XLSX, col_types = "text")
practice_names <- keywords |>
  filter(!practice_group %in% c("geography", names(OUTCOME_LABELS))) |>
  distinct(practice_group, practice_label)
PRACTICE_NAMES <- setNames(practice_names$practice_label, practice_names$practice_group)

counts <- read_cols(FILE_SEARCH_COUNTS, c("search_id", "practice_group", "outcome", "hits",
                                          "counted_on")) |>
  mutate(hits = as.integer(hits))
search_date <- format(as.Date(max(counts$counted_on)), "%d %B %Y")

records <- read_cols(FILE_SEARCH_MATCHED, c("record_id", "doi", "is_oa", "abstract_source"))
# Abstracts found beyond OpenAlex and the 2022 refs, by R/01_search/fill_abstracts.R.
abstracts_found <- sum(!records$abstract_source %in% c("openalex", "wb2022", "none", NA))

# A person's QC decision overrides the model's. Spelling slips ("exlude")
# are read by their first letters. An exclusion the person confirmed keeps
# the model's reason; one the person made is counted as a QC exclusion.
screen <- read_cols(FILE_SCREEN, c("record_id", "qc_sample", "qc_decision", "decision",
                                   "decision_rule", "found_by", "wb_positive", "wb_africa")) |>
  left_join(records, by = "record_id") |>
  mutate(
    qc = tolower(trimws(coalesce(qc_decision, ""))),
    qc = case_when(startsWith(qc, "inc") ~ "include", startsWith(qc, "ex") ~ "exclude",
                   startsWith(qc, "uns") ~ "unsure", TRUE ~ NA_character_),
    checked = !is.na(qc_sample) & !is.na(qc),
    final = ifelse(checked, qc, decision),
    group = case_when(
      checked & final == "exclude" & decision != "exclude" ~ "qc_excluded",
      final == "exclude" ~ unname(EXCLUDE_RULES[decision_rule]),
      final == "include" ~ "included",
      decision_rule == "unsure: title only" ~ "title_only",
      TRUE ~ "unsure"
    ),
    open_access = is_oa %in% "TRUE",
    has_doi = !is.na(doi),
    wb_africa_included = wb_positive %in% "TRUE" & wb_africa %in% "TRUE"
  ) |>
  # Records with no abstract anywhere are left out of this report for now.
  filter(group != "title_only")

# One row per record and search that found it.
screen_long <- screen |>
  select(record_id, found_by, group, open_access, has_doi) |>
  tidyr::separate_rows(found_by, sep = ";[[:space:]]*") |>
  mutate(practice = sub("__.*$", "", found_by), outcome = sub("^.*__", "", found_by))

#' The screening counts for one practice and outcome ("all" for every one). A
#' record found by several of the chosen searches is screened once.
screen_counts <- function(p, o) {
  d <- screen_long
  s <- counts
  if (p != "all") { d <- filter(d, practice == p); s <- filter(s, practice_group == p) }
  if (o != "all") { d <- filter(d, outcome == o); s <- filter(s, outcome == o) }
  u <- distinct(d, record_id, .keep_all = TRUE)
  g <- as.list(table(factor(u$group, levels = names(SCREEN_GROUPS))))
  c(list(searches = nrow(s), hits = sum(s$hits), found = nrow(d), screened = nrow(u),
         duplicates = nrow(d) - nrow(u), excluded = sum(unlist(g[EXCLUDE_GROUPS])),
         included_oa = sum(u$open_access & u$group == "included"),
         included_doi = sum(u$has_doi & u$group == "included")), g)
}
overall <- screen_counts("all", "all")
fmt <- function(x) format(x, big.mark = ",")
```

```{r at-a-glance, results = "asis"}
steps <- list(

)
cards <- vapply(steps, function(s) sprintf(
  '<div class="step %s"><div class="step-n">%s</div><div><b>%s</b><div class="step-status">%s</div><div class="step-note">%s</div></div></div>',
  ifelse(startsWith(s[3], "Done"), "done", "todo"), s[1], s[2], s[3], s[4]), "")
cat('<div class="steps">', paste(cards, collapse = ""), '</div>')
```

## 1. The 2022 World Bank data

The 2022 World Bank NbS review extracted costs, returns and adoption from studies in low and middle income countries. Cleaned for CC4A (`data/wb_nbs_extraction_2022_cc4a.xlsx`), it is the starting point: the papers it holds need no new search, and the papers its reviewers included are used below to test the screening.

### Scope of the data

The extraction covered low and middle income countries everywhere; this page keeps the **`r n_distinct(af$StudyID)` African studies** (`r format(nrow(af), big.mark = ",")` observations) that test a CC4A practice. Values are as extracted in 2022, in each paper's own currency and prices; nothing is converted.

```{r scope-map}
by_country <- af |>
  mutate(country = strsplit(Country, "[/;,] *")) |>
  unnest(country) |>
  mutate(country = trimws(country)) |>
  group_by(country) |>
  summarise(studies = n_distinct(StudyID), observations = n(), .groups = "drop")
plot_ly(by_country, type = "choropleth", locations = ~country, locationmode = "country names",
        z = ~studies, colorscale = "Blues", reversescale = TRUE, height = 480,
        text = ~paste0(country, ": ", studies, " studies, ", observations, " observations"),
        hoverinfo = "text", colorbar = list(title = "Studies", x = 0.85, len = 0.6)) |>
  layout(title = list(text = "Studies by country", x = 0),
         geo = list(scope = "africa", showframe = FALSE, showcountries = TRUE),
         margin = list(l = 0, r = 0, t = 40, b = 0))
```

```{r scope-bars, fig.height = 6}
per_outcome <- af |>

bscols(
```

### How many years does each paper report an outcome for?

Choose an outcome. The chart counts the papers reporting it by the number of years their data cover, and colours them by how those years are reported: **a separate value for each season** or **for each year** (these show change over time), **one value pooled over the years** (does not), or a single year. Tick a number of years to list those papers in the table.

```{r years}
paper_outcome <- money |>
  group_by(StudyID, paper, Outcome) |>
  summarise(
    Country = first(Country),
    practices = paste(sort(unique(unlist(strsplit(practices, "; ")))), collapse = "; "),
    unit = paste(sort(unique(unit)), collapse = ", "),
    years_covered = length(unique(unlist(years))),
    separate_years = n_distinct(year_first[n_years == 1]),
    separate_points = n_distinct(Measurement_Year[n_years == 1]),
    seasonal = any(!is.na(season)),
    first_year = suppressWarnings(min(year_first, na.rm = TRUE)),
    last_year = suppressWarnings(max(year_last, na.rm = TRUE)),
    items = items_text(pick(all_of(COST_ITEMS))),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  filter(years_covered > 0) |>
  mutate(
    how = case_when(separate_points >= 2 & seasonal ~ "A separate value for each season",
                    separate_years >= 2 ~ "A separate value for each year",
                    years_covered == 1 ~ "One year",
                    TRUE ~ "One value pooled over the years"),
    how = factor(how, levels = names(HOW_COLOURS)),
    period = ifelse(first_year == last_year, as.character(first_year),
                    paste(first_year, last_year, sep = " to ")),
    time_points = ifelse(how %in% c("A separate value for each season",
                                    "A separate value for each year"), separate_points, 1L)
  ) |>
  arrange(Outcome, desc(time_points), desc(years_covered))

sd_po <- SharedData$new(
  paper_outcome |> transmute(Outcome, years_covered, time_points, how, period, paper,
                             practices, unit, items),
  group = "paper_outcome"
)
htmltools::tagList(
  bscols(
    widths = c(6, 6),
    filter_select("po_outcome", "Outcome", sd_po, ~Outcome, multiple = FALSE),
    filter_checkbox("po_years", "Years covered", sd_po, ~years_covered, inline = TRUE)
  ),
  plot_ly(sd_po, x = ~years_covered, color = ~how, colors = HOW_COLOURS, type = "histogram",
          xbins = list(start = 0.5, size = 1), height = 360) |>
    layout(barmode = "stack",
           xaxis = list(title = "Years of data in the paper", dtick = 1,
                        range = c(0.5, max(paper_outcome$years_covered) + 0.5)),
           yaxis = list(title = "Papers"),
           legend = list(orientation = "h", y = -0.3)),
  datatable(sd_po, rownames = FALSE, class = "compact stripe hover", width = "100%",
            colnames = c("Outcome", "Years", "Time points", "How the years are reported", "Period",
                         "Paper", "Practice", "Unit", "Cost items included"),
            options = list(pageLength = 10, dom = "tip", autoWidth = FALSE,
                           columnDefs = list(list(visible = FALSE, targets = 0),
                                             list(width = "40px", targets = c(1, 2)),
                                             list(width = "300px", targets = 5))))
)
```

### Plot a paper over time

Choose an outcome and a paper (the table above lists the papers that report each outcome; if the chart is empty, the paper does not report that outcome). **Solid blue lines are treatment arms, grey dashed lines are control arms.** Seasons are separate points within their year. A value pooled over several years is a **hollow point in the middle of its period** (hover to see the years it covers); it is not joined to other points, because it is not a value for any one year. Hover for the arm, value, year or season and the cost items.

```{r plot-paper}
# Each extracted row pairs a treatment arm with a control arm. Both become
# points; an arm compared with several controls, or a control shared by
# several arms, is kept once, and an arm used in both roles in one paper is
# kept as a treatment arm.
make_points <- function(d, role, arm, value) {
  d |>
    filter(!is.na({{ value }}), !is.na(year_first)) |>
    transmute(StudyID, paper, Outcome, unit, where, items, Measurement_Year, n_years,
              year_first, year_last, season, arm = {{ arm }}, role = role, value = {{ value }})
}
trt_pts <- make_points(money, "Treatment", Treatment_Name, value_trt)
con_pts <- make_points(money, "Control", Control_Name, value_con) |>
  anti_join(distinct(trt_pts, StudyID, Outcome, arm), by = c("StudyID", "Outcome", "arm"))

pts <- bind_rows(trt_pts, con_pts) |>
  distinct(StudyID, Outcome, unit, where, Measurement_Year, arm, role, value, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  mutate(
    pooled = n_years > 1,
    # Seasons sit within their year: season 1 at the year, season 2 a third
    # of the way through, season 3 two thirds.
    x = ifelse(pooled, (year_first + year_last) / 2,
               year_first + (coalesce(season, 1L) - 1) / 3),
    when = case_when(pooled ~ paste0(year_first, " to ", year_last, " (one value for the whole period)"),
                     !is.na(season) ~ paste0(year_first, ", season ", season),
                     TRUE ~ as.character(year_first)),
    arm_where = ifelse(nzchar(where), paste0(arm, " (", where, ")"), arm),
    # A pooled value is its own trace, so it is never joined by a line.
    line = paste(role, arm_where, ifelse(pooled, paste(Measurement_Year, value), "series"), sep = " :: "),
    marker_symbol = ifelse(pooled, "Pooled over years", "Single year or season"),
    hover = paste0("<b>", arm_where, "</b> (", tolower(role), " arm)<br>",
                   Outcome, ": ", format(value, big.mark = ","), " ", unit,
                   "<br>", when, "<br>Cost items: ", items)
  ) |>
  arrange(Outcome, paper, line, x) |>
  select(arm_where, role, when, value, unit, items, everything())

# The paper picker shows how many years each paper's cost and return data
# cover, and lists the papers with the most years first.
paper_years <- money |>
  group_by(paper) |>
  summarise(years = length(unique(unlist(years))), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(paper_label = paste0("[", years, " yr] ", paper)) |>
  arrange(desc(years), paper)
pts <- pts |>
  left_join(select(paper_years, paper, paper_label), by = "paper") |>
  mutate(paper_label = factor(paper_label, levels = paper_years$paper_label))

sd_pts <- SharedData$new(pts, key = ~paste(Outcome, line, x, value), group = "points")

# Open on the default outcome and the paper with the most separate time points for it.
default_paper <- paper_outcome |>
  filter(Outcome == DEFAULT_OUTCOME) |>
  arrange(desc(time_points), desc(years_covered)) |>
  pull(paper) |>
  first()
default_paper <- paper_years$paper_label[paper_years$paper == default_paper]

htmltools::tagList(
  bscols(
    widths = c(4, 8),
    filter_select("pt_outcome", "Outcome", sd_pts, ~Outcome, multiple = FALSE),
    filter_select("pt_paper", "Paper (years of data)", sd_pts, ~paper_label, multiple = FALSE)
  ),
  plot_ly(sd_pts, x = ~x, y = ~value, split = ~line, color = ~role,
          colors = c(Treatment = COL_TREATMENT, Control = COL_CONTROL),
          linetype = ~role, linetypes = c(Treatment = "solid", Control = "dash"),
          symbol = ~marker_symbol,
          symbols = c("Single year or season" = "circle", "Pooled over years" = "circle-open"),
          type = "scatter", mode = "lines+markers", marker = list(size = 9),
          text = ~hover, hoverinfo = "text", showlegend = FALSE, height = 460) |>
    layout(xaxis = list(title = "Year (seasons as points within the year)", dtick = 1,
                        tickangle = 0),
           yaxis = list(title = "Value (paper's own currency and unit)", rangemode = "tozero"),
           margin = list(t = 20)),
  datatable(sd_pts, rownames = FALSE, class = "compact stripe hover", width = "100%",
            colnames = setNames(c("arm_where", "role", "when", "value", "unit", "items"),
                                c("Treatment / control", "Role", "Year or season", "Value", "Unit",
                                  "Cost items included")),
            options = list(pageLength = 10, dom = "tip",
                           columnDefs = list(list(visible = FALSE,
                                                  targets = seq(6, ncol(pts) - 1)))))
)
```

```{r defaults, results = "asis"}
# crosstalk has no default selection and does not link one dropdown to
# another. This script (1) sets the outcome and paper filters on load, so the
# page does not open with every outcome and paper drawn at once, and (2) keeps
# the paper dropdown to the papers that report the chosen outcome, most years
# first, switching to the first of them when the current paper has none.
papers_by_outcome <- pts |>
  distinct(Outcome, paper_label) |>
  mutate(paper_label = as.character(paper_label)) |>
  arrange(Outcome, match(paper_label, paper_years$paper_label)) |>
  group_by(Outcome) |>
  summarise(papers = list(paper_label), .groups = "drop")
papers_by_outcome <- setNames(papers_by_outcome$papers, papers_by_outcome$Outcome)

cat(sprintf('<script>
window.addEventListener("load", function () {
  var papersByOutcome = %3$s;
  var tries = 0;
  (function setup() {
    var po = document.querySelector("#po_outcome select");
    var outcome = document.querySelector("#pt_outcome select");
    var paper = document.querySelector("#pt_paper select");
    if (!(po && po.selectize && outcome && outcome.selectize && paper && paper.selectize)) {
      if (tries++ < 50) setTimeout(setup, 100);
      return;
    }
    var allPapers = Object.assign({}, paper.selectize.options);
    function limitPapers(chosen) {
      var sel = paper.selectize;
      var keep = papersByOutcome[chosen] || Object.keys(allPapers);
      var current = sel.getValue();
      sel.clearOptions(true);
      keep.forEach(function (v) { if (allPapers[v]) sel.addOption(allPapers[v]); });
      sel.refreshOptions(false);
      sel.setValue(keep.indexOf(current) >= 0 ? current : keep[0]);
    }
    outcome.selectize.on("change", function (v) { limitPapers(v); });
    po.selectize.setValue(%1$s);
    outcome.selectize.setValue(%1$s);
    limitPapers(%1$s);
    paper.selectize.setValue(%2$s);
  })();
});
</script>', jsonlite::toJSON(DEFAULT_OUTCOME, auto_unbox = TRUE),
            jsonlite::toJSON(default_paper, auto_unbox = TRUE),
            jsonlite::toJSON(papers_by_outcome, auto_unbox = FALSE)))
```

### What the costs include

For each cost item, how many papers' cost figures include it, leave it out, or do not say, across all cost outcomes (variable, total, labour ...). A paper counts as including an item when any of its cost figures does. Costs that leave out labour or land are not comparable with costs that include them.

```{r cost-items}
cost_items <- money |>
  filter(Outcome %in% COST_OUTCOMES) |>
  select(StudyID, all_of(COST_ITEMS)) |>
  pivot_longer(all_of(COST_ITEMS), names_to = "item", values_to = "flag") |>
  group_by(StudyID, item) |>
  summarise(status = case_when(any(grepl("^[(]?yes", flag, ignore.case = TRUE)) ~ "Included",
                               any(grepl("^no", flag, ignore.case = TRUE)) ~ "Not included",
                               TRUE ~ "Not recorded"),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  count(item, status) |>
  mutate(item = unname(setNames(COST_ITEM_SHORT, COST_ITEMS)[item]),
         status = factor(status, levels = c("Included", "Not included", "Not recorded")))
item_order <- cost_items |>
  filter(status == "Included") |>
  arrange(n) |>
  pull(item)
item_order <- c(setdiff(unique(cost_items$item), item_order), item_order)
n_cost_papers <- n_distinct(money$StudyID[money$Outcome %in% COST_OUTCOMES])

plot_ly(cost_items, y = ~factor(item, levels = item_order), x = ~n, color = ~status,
        colors = c("Included" = "#1f6fb4", "Not included" = "#fdae61", "Not recorded" = "#d9d9d9"),
        type = "bar", orientation = "h", height = 380,
        text = ~paste0(item, ": ", n, " paper(s), ", tolower(status)),
        hoverinfo = "text", textposition = "none") |>
  layout(barmode = "stack",
         title = list(text = paste0("Cost items in the ", n_cost_papers, " papers reporting costs"), x = 0),
         xaxis = list(title = "Papers"), yaxis = list(title = ""),
         legend = list(orientation = "h", y = -0.2))
```

## 2. The practices

The review's practice vocabulary, written by Pete Steward (`catalogues/vocab_practices.csv`; the full definitions and rules are in `docs/synthesis/01-practice-definitions.md`). Each practice has a definition, the farming system it applies to, the comparator a study must use, its ERA practice codes, and what does not count as the practice. Extraction records every value against one of these codes. The OpenAlex search below groups its keywords into `r length(PRACTICE_NAMES)` search practices (`docs/synthesis/key-words.xlsx`), which are broader than this list. Click a practice to see its definition; practices not taken forward or out of scope are listed so they can be named as reasons to exclude.

```{r vocabulary, results = "asis"}
SCOPE_LABELS <- c(in_scope = "In scope", not_taken_forward = "Not taken forward",
                  out_of_scope = "Out of scope")
vocab <- readr::read_csv(FILE_VOCAB_PRACTICES, col_types = readr::cols(.default = "c"),
                         na = "", show_col_types = FALSE)
esc <- function(x) htmltools::htmlEscape(dplyr::coalesce(x, ""))
field <- function(name, value) {
  if (is.na(value) || !nzchar(value)) "" else
    sprintf('<div class="vfield"><span class="vname">%s</span> %s</div>', name, esc(value))
}
for (sc in names(SCOPE_LABELS)) {
  v <- vocab[vocab$scope == sc, ]
  cat(sprintf('<h4 class="vgroup">%s (%d)</h4>', SCOPE_LABELS[[sc]], nrow(v)))
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(v))) {
    r <- v[i, ]
    cat(sprintf(
      '<details class="vpractice"><summary><b>%s</b> <code>%s</code>%s%s</summary>%s%s%s%s%s</details>',
      esc(r$label), esc(r$practice_code),
      if (r$pilot %in% "yes") ' <span class="vpilot">Pilot</span>' else "",
      if (!is.na(r$system)) paste0(' <span class="vsystem">', esc(r$system), "</span>") else "",
      field("Definition", r$definition), field("Comparator", r$comparator),
      field("ERA codes", gsub(";", "; ", r$era_codes)),
      field("Does not count, and bundles", r$notes),
      field("Crosswalk", r$crosswalk)))
  }
}
```

## 3. The OpenAlex search

The 2022 data are not enough on their own, so the literature was searched again in OpenAlex on `r search_date`: **`r overall$searches` searches**, one for each of the `r length(PRACTICE_NAMES)` practices and the three outcome blocks (adoption; costs, returns and incentives; carbon finance), each combined with the Africa terms and limited to papers from 1990 to 2026. The search terms are in `docs/synthesis/key-words.xlsx`. Together the searches returned `r fmt(overall$hits)` hits; many papers are found by more than one search, which leaves **`r fmt(nrow(records))` unique records**.

```{r search-heatmap, fig.height = 6}
hit_matrix <- counts |>
  mutate(practice = factor(PRACTICE_NAMES[practice_group], levels = rev(PRACTICE_NAMES)),
         outcome = factor(OUTCOME_LABELS[outcome], levels = OUTCOME_LABELS))
plot_ly(hit_matrix, x = ~outcome, y = ~practice, z = ~log10(pmax(hits, 1)), type = "heatmap",
        colorscale = list(c(0, "#f7fbff"), c(1, "#6baed6")), showscale = FALSE, height = 560,
        text = ~paste0(practice, ", ", tolower(outcome), ": ", fmt(hits), " hits"),
        hoverinfo = "text", xgap = 2, ygap = 2) |>
  add_annotations(x = ~outcome, y = ~practice, text = ~fmt(hits), showarrow = FALSE,
                  font = list(color = "#222")) |>
  layout(title = list(text = "OpenAlex hits per practice and outcome", x = 0),
         xaxis = list(title = "", side = "top"), yaxis = list(title = ""),
         margin = list(l = 10, t = 70))
```

## 4. Title and abstract screening

Every record was screened on its title and abstract by a GPT model (gpt-4.1-mini), following the ERA screening workflow. The model answers one question per criterion: is the study in Africa, does it study one of the practices, does it report costs, adoption or carbon income, and what kind of study is it. Code then turns the answers into include, exclude or unsure, so every decision names the criterion that set it. Papers the 2022 reviewers included were shown to the model as examples. OpenAlex holds no abstract for some records; `R/01_search/fill_abstracts.R` found **`r fmt(abstracts_found)`** of them elsewhere (Europe PMC, Semantic Scholar, Crossref and the publishers' own pages), and those records were screened on their abstract.

### Each search

One row per search: what OpenAlex returned, how many of those records were screened, and where they ended up, with the person's QC decisions in place of the model's. A record found by more than one search is counted in each, so the rows add up to more than the `r fmt(overall$screened)` records screened. Across all searches: **`r fmt(overall$included)` included** for full text, `r fmt(overall$excluded)` excluded, `r fmt(overall$unsure)` unsure, for a person. Sort or filter by any column.

```{r screen-table}
per_search <- counts |>
  transmute(practice = practice_group, outcome) |>
  mutate(c = Map(screen_counts, practice, outcome)) |>
  transmute(
    Practice = PRACTICE_NAMES[practice],
    Outcome = OUTCOME_LABELS[outcome],
    `OpenAlex hits` = vapply(c, `[[`, 1L, "hits"),
    Screened = vapply(c, `[[`, 1L, "screened"),
    Excluded = vapply(c, `[[`, 1L, "excluded"),
    Unsure = vapply(c, `[[`, 1L, "unsure"),
    Included = vapply(c, `[[`, 1L, "included"),
    `% included` = round(100 * Included / pmax(Screened, 1))
  )
datatable(per_search, rownames = FALSE, class = "compact stripe hover", width = "100%",
          filter = "top", options = list(pageLength = 15, dom = "tip", order = list(list(6, "desc")))) |>
  formatRound(c("OpenAlex hits", "Screened", "Excluded", "Unsure", "Included"), digits = 0)
```

### Checking the model: the person's QC

A person checked three samples of the model's decisions from the title and abstract, with the model's decision in view: a random 50 of its includes, a random 100 of its excludes, and every record it was unsure about that had an abstract. Their decisions replace the model's in the table above.

```{r qc}
qc_rows <- screen |> filter(checked)
qc_table <- qc_rows |>
  mutate(Sample = recode(qc_sample, "check include" = "Random sample of the model's includes",
                         "check exclude" = "Random sample of the model's excludes",
                         "decide unsure" = "All the model's unsure records with an abstract")) |>
  group_by(Sample) |>
  summarise(Checked = n(),
            `Person: include` = sum(qc == "include"),
            `Person: exclude` = sum(qc == "exclude"),
            `Agreed with the model` = if (all(decision == "unsure")) "n/a"
                                      else paste0(sum(qc == decision), " (", round(100 * mean(qc == decision)), "%)"),
            .groups = "drop")
knitr::kable(qc_table, align = "lrrrr")

inc <- qc_rows |> filter(qc_sample == "check include")
exc <- qc_rows |> filter(qc_sample == "check exclude")
missed <- sum(exc$qc != "exclude")
wb <- screen |> filter(wb_africa_included)
```

- **Includes.** The person kept `r sum(inc$qc == "include")` of the `r nrow(inc)` sampled includes (`r round(100 * mean(inc$qc == "include"))`%). The full-text screen will catch more of the includes that do not hold up.
- **Excludes.** The person would have kept `r missed` of the `r nrow(exc)` sampled excludes. `r if (missed == 0) paste0("With none in ", nrow(exc), ", the share of relevant papers among all ", fmt(sum(screen$decision == "exclude")), " excludes is, with 95% confidence, below about ", round(300 / nrow(exc)), "%.") else ""`
- **Unsure.** Of the `r sum(qc_rows$qc_sample == "decide unsure")` unsure records with an abstract, the person included `r sum(qc_rows$qc_sample == "decide unsure" & qc_rows$qc == "include")`.
- **Against the 2022 reviewers.** The search found `r nrow(wb)` African papers the 2022 reviewers included. The screening keeps `r sum(wb$final != "exclude")` of them (`r round(100 * mean(wb$final != "exclude"))`%) for full text or for a person to decide.

## 5. Next steps

1. **Full texts through Zotero.** Send the `r fmt(overall$included)` included records to a shared Zotero library through the Zotero web API, by DOI where there is one (`r fmt(overall$included_doi)` have a DOI). Zotero then fetches the PDFs it can find; `r fmt(overall$included_oa)` are open access according to OpenAlex. What Zotero cannot find becomes a short list to get through library access.
2. **Full-text screening.** Check each PDF against the same criteria with the full paper in hand, recording a reason for every exclusion.
3. **Data extraction.** Extract into the template (`docs/synthesis/extraction_template.xlsx`), as piloted on five papers: costs, returns and adoption with their units, years and the cost items they include, each value with its page and a verbatim quote.
4. **Extraction QC.** A second person extracts a random sample of papers independently; the two are compared field by field, and values are checked against their quotes.
